title: Parliamentary and presidential systems compared
examples: What is the difference between a prime minister and a president?
How is a prime minister chosen?

explain.say: How does a country pick its top leader? Some let you vote for a president directly. Others let you vote for a parliament, and parliament picks the leader. Look at the board: parliamentary on the left, presidential on the right.

explain.say: See the left side glow. In a parliamentary system you vote for members of parliament. The leader who has most of them on side becomes prime minister, and stays only while parliament trusts them. India, Japan, the UK and Canada work like this. Who leads your country?

explain.say: Now the right side. In a presidential system you vote for the president directly, separately from the congress that makes laws. The president serves a fixed term: four years in the USA and Brazil, six in Mexico. Can you name another presidential country?

explain.say: Let's zoom in on how a prime minister is chosen. Voters elect members, seats are counted, a majority backs a leader, and that leader becomes prime minister. Look at the last step: lose parliament's trust and you lose the job. Surprised?

faq.q: How is a prime minister chosen?
faq.a: In most parliamentary systems the prime minister is the person who can win the support of a majority in parliament, usually the leader of the biggest party or coalition.
In presidential systems voters choose the president in a separate election. Brazil and Mexico count the national vote directly; the USA uses an Electoral College based on states.

faq.q: Can a prime minister be removed?
faq.a: Yes. Parliament can pass a vote of no confidence, or the prime minister's own party can replace them, without a general election.
asks: How does a prime minister lose power?

faq.a: It mixes both: an elected president shares power with a prime minister who needs parliament's support. France and Portugal work this way.

Each has trade-offs. Parliamentary systems can change leaders quickly and link government closely to lawmakers; presidential systems give a directly chosen leader and a fixed term. Successful democracies use both.
asks: Is a president better than a prime minister?

facts: In 2022 the UK had three prime ministers: Boris Johnson, Liz Truss and Rishi Sunak.
A Mexican president serves a single six-year term and cannot be re-elected.
